messages:
maria_ml: Heads-up — canary shows a decode path regression after we flipped the paged-FlashAttention variant. p99 up ~18% on small-batch interactive workloads. Anyone on call for a quick triage? :eyes:

 tim_kernels: Can you paste the benchmark config and numbers? small-batch decode covers a lot of production traffic so we should be precise.

 maria_ml: Repro steps: ran bench suite on canary (gpu-a, cuda12). Model: redwood-3b-fused. Config: batch sizes 1..4, seq_in 32, seq_out 64, decode streaming. Command: `./bench/run_decode.sh --model redwood-3b-fused --variant paged-flash --batch-range 1,4 --seq-in 32 --seq-out 64 --runs 150`

 tim_kernels: Paste of trimmed output:
```
baseline (fused-attn): batch=1 p50=23ms p95=48ms p99=89ms
paged-flash (new):  batch=1 p50=25ms p95=62ms p99=105ms
batch=2 baseline p99=72ms  paged-flash p99=83ms
batch=4 baseline p99=110ms paged-flash p99=115ms
```
This is consistent with your 18% p99 hit at batch=1.

 raj_serving: Kernel selector logs look interesting. For decode we were routing to `flash_paged_variant` when seq<=128 regardless of batch. Selector trace snippet: `rule: if seq<=128 -> choose=flash_paged` and no special-casing for batch==1. I think the paged variant has higher setup/copy cost for tiny batches because it does a KV page allocation and memcpy on prefill->decode transition.

 sarah_perf: I instrumented the canary with nvtx markers. Short summary: paged-flash spends ~0.9ms extra on page table setup + 1.2ms in device->device memcpy for KV reorg on every decode step for small-batch streams. Kernel timings (avg single step, batch=1):
```
prefill kernel (flash): 12.3ms
decode step kernel (paged-flash): 3.1ms
kv_reorg/copy overhead: 1.2ms
kernel-launch/setup: 0.9ms
==> effective step = 5.2ms vs fused decode step=3.5ms
```
so the kv reorg and extra setup are the culprits.

 tim_kernels: Two quick mitigations we can do: 1) adjust selector to prefer fused for batch<=2 on decode path, 2) add a cheap fastpath that skips page-reorg when KV is contiguous (detectable via header bit). Option 1 is simplest short-term.

 dave_ops: Also saw an increase in tail latency in prod traces after canary roll. Continuous batching heuristic is aggregating requests into microbatches and the microbatcher has max_delay_ms=5 currently; that increases the chance of creating batch=1 decode steps if traffic is bursty. Trying max_delay_ms=2 reduced observed microbatch size variance and helped in local sim. Not a full fix but reduces exposure.

 maria_ml: TL;DR — cause: paged-flash variant has higher per-step setup/copy cost that pays off at larger batch/seq but regresses small-batch decode. Proposed immediate action: revert selector rule for decode -> prefer fused when batch<=2 OR when request latency budget < 50ms. Who can push the selector change + smoke test?

 tim_kernels: I'll open a tiny rollback PR to the selector heuristics: change rule to `if route==decode and batch<=2 -> prefer=fused_attn` and add a metric emission `kernel_choice_reason=small_batch_decode` for monitoring. Will run bench with 200 runs. ETA 1.5h.

 raj_serving: I'll add a canary that emits KV fragmentation counters and a flag `kv_contiguous_fastpath` so that when set we can test perf of paged-flash without reorgs.

 infra-bot: deploy-bot posted: "canary updated: selector-heuristic-tweak to gpu-a pool (roll 10%)"

 sarah_perf: After selector change in local run (sim):
```
batch=1 fused p99=88ms -> matches baseline (no regression)
batch=4 paged-flash still wins for throughput p99=112ms
```
I'll run extended overnight suite and upload full traces.

 maria_ml: Great. Action items: tim -> PR and bench (owner). raj -> kv counters + fastpath flag. sarah -> extended perf run + traces. dave -> try reducing microbatch delay on prod sim. I'll track cluster-level SLOs for the next 24h. If regressions persist we disable paged-flash on decode by default.

 tim_kernels: PR link: https://git.company/repo/p/r/1327 (draft). Bench command used: `./bench/run_decode.sh --variant selector-fix --runs 200 --log-level perf`

 maria_ml: Thanks all. Filing follow-up ticket for kernel selector policy doc so this heuristic isn't ad-hoc next time. :thumbsup:
